name: Pressure-pop recycler
subtitle: a chamber that pops glued phones apart

effects.effect: carbon dioxide squeezed past its critical point seeps into glue like a gas and dissolves like a liquid
when pressure drops, the dissolved gas froths into bubbles inside the glue

effect: carbon dioxide squeezed past its critical point seeps into glue like a gas and dissolves like a liquid
how: Phones and laptops are glued so tightly that recyclers shred them whole, losing most of the cobalt, rare-earth magnets and gold in the dust. Here whole devices sit in a steel chamber full of carbon dioxide squeezed until it is neither gas nor liquid, which soaks into every glue line; when the pressure is dropped in a second, the gas froths inside the glue and the device falls apart into battery, screen, board and magnets, ready to sort.
obstacle: The chamber must hold about 75 times normal air pressure, and the sudden drop must not crack a lithium battery into a fire.
why: Taking devices apart is the bottleneck of e-waste recovery; this undoes every glue at once.
real: Supercritical CO2 with rapid depressurisation is studied for delaminating PCBs and multilayer films, and old patents use CO2 to dissolve adhesives, but no scCO2 adhesive-foaming disassembly of whole phones was found.
